items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: Tony Parenti was there, and Tony Parenti was an Italian guy, and so forth.

ctx.x: That’s a good point. And depending on what history writer you read, sometimes you’ll get that opinion and sometimes you won’t.

Well I mean if you read about the early history of the music from the guys who actually did it, for instance, Alan Lomax’s book about Jelly Roll Morton called Mr. Jelly Lord. Jelly Roll Morton. It’s basically taken from tapes of Jelly Roll Morton talking about the music, and him saying well yeah, we listened to the European musicians and we had such-and-such and Tony Parenti was there, and Tony Parenti was an Italian guy, and so forth. And that’s what it was. It was a combination of the African sounds and rhythms…
uniquely there because of the combination of the different ideas and the different musical concepts.
